To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glucose depletion induces a tight junction in an adenocarcinomatous colon epithelial cell line, HCT-116.
glucose depletion of a colon adenocarinoma cell line (HCT-116) induces enterocytic differentiation of the cells.

glucose deprivation of HCT-116 cells grown under permissive differentiation induces the formation of a functional tight junction, which is not observed when the cells are grown under standard culture condition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the tight junction in a cell line that is a model of the intestinal epithelium.
the establishment and functional characterization of the tight junction in a human colonic adenocarcinomic cell line.
the study of the molecular and functional characteristics of tight junctions in differentiated colon cancer cells, and their possible role in the process of tumor invasion and metastasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the glucose-deprived medium is able to induce a functional tight junction, which is not present under standard culture conditions.
tight junction formation and function is not dependent on glucose metabolism, but rather on a specific inosine-mediated differentiation process.

tight junctions are formed in a differentiated cell line, and that they are functional, as shown by the presence of occludin and its hyperphosphorylation, and by the increase of the transepithelial resistence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glucose depletion of the culture medium is a useful method to induce the differentiation of the colon adenocarcineoma cell line HCT-116, and to study the assembly of the tight junctions.
glucose depletion of the culture medium induced a differentiation process in HCT-116 cells characterized by the formation of a tight junction, and the expression of a brush border marker.

glucose depletion of the culture medium is a simple, reproducible and efficient tool for the induction of an enterocytic phenotype and the formation of functional tight junctions in a colonic epithelial cell line.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HCT-116 cells can be differentiated into enterocytes in vitro.
tight junction assembly is a complex process that requires the interaction of multiple proteins and that the assembly of the tight junction is dependent on the presence of glucose.

the HCT-116 colon cancer cell line, when cultured under differentiation conditions, can be a valuable model to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the formation of the tight junction in intestinal epithelium.
